Composio holds every app login

One Composio account (org wearenumber1, signed in as alex@increaseroas.com) holds every app login. It has two doors into the same logins: the `composio` command (a CLI, meaning a command typed in a terminal) wherever a terminal exists, and the Composio app's tools in chats that have no terminal.
One place to fix a login, and every AI gets the same thing. Both doors see the same logins, so there is never a second copy to keep in step.

1Password holds every key
Every API key lives in the 1Password vault Connectors, shared with Alex, Manny and Anthony. Scripts read it with robot logins (1Password service accounts: logins for scripts that need no Touch ID).
One home per key. A key that lives in two places drifts, and a copy in a file gets leaked.

Every secret an AI needs is in Connectors

Every secret an AI or script needs lives in the Connectors vault, which the connectors-sync robots read. Nothing an AI needs lives in Employee or Private, the default Shared vault, 'Local Vault (operator secrets)' or a 1Password Environment. Agents read 1Password only through the Keychain robot; making robots, Connect servers or vault grants is Alex's (a security setting). Javar's and the agent team's own vaults stay as they are (their fence).

Robots, 1Password Connect and Composio's 1Password can never reach the built-in Personal, Private or Employee vault or the default Shared vault, and 'Local Vault (operator secrets)' is granted to no robot. Anything outside the robots' reach is read as Alex through the 1Password app, which asks for Touch ID. One exception: the robots' recovery tokens stay in 'Local Vault (operator secrets)', so no robot can read another robot's token (least privilege).

A key goes from 1Password into Composio only through the key mover script (push_key_to_composio.py). Keys never go in chat, files or logs, and scripts never print them.

Composio then serves the app to every AI without anyone handling the key again. 1Password stays the source and Composio keeps a working copy. All current Composio logins were created after Composio's breach disclosure of 2026-05-21.

Claude Code (terminal and the desktop Code tab)

The `composio` command first: `composio search "<task>"`, then `composio execute` (and `composio proxy` for raw API calls with the stored login). The claude.ai Composio connector arrives on its own and reaches the same account; use it only when the command can't run. Inside the Claude Code sandbox (the safety box Claude Code runs commands in), `composio execute` works, at most warning that it can't write its cache; `composio search` and `--get-schema` fail there because they write ~/.composio, so run those outside it.

The `op` command (1Password's CLI). Interactive work signs in with Touch ID through the 1Password app; scripts use the robot login; values are piped to their target and never printed (the key mover, `op run`, `op inject`). `op` fails inside the Claude Code sandbox, so it runs outside it.

Proven 2026-10-01: `composio whoami` shows alex@increaseroas.com and org wearenumber1, and the connector and the command see the same logins. The composio@composio plugin's self-updating hook (a script the app runs by itself) is pinned to marketplace tag v0.2.4 since 2026-10-01 (I15). Headless live tests on 2026-10-01 were BLOCKED: the terminal CLI (2.1.251) was signed out ("OAuth session expired"). By about 20:46Z it was on 2.1.287 and signed in with claude.ai, and it syncs the claude.ai connectors. The conductor then ran the same tests as Claude Code subagents in the signed-in desktop app: T1–T6 PASS, including T2 (a Gmail draft created and trashed, never sent) and T3 (a 1Password read through the Keychain token and op, hashed, with no value shown); T7 PASS on the terminal and, after the restart, on the desktop. On 2026-10-02 the terminal ran T1–T6 headless: all 6 PASS (T2 under the headless guard rule), and the fresh-session guard check passed (Tests tab).

1. Copy the key
